stemi.title: What a heart attack looks like, inside the heart and on the ECG
stemi.post: We block the LAD, the artery on the front of the heart, and watch 1 month of a heart attack in 25 seconds: tall T waves, ST elevation, Q waves, flipped T waves. Simulated with ECG Studio, a free 3D heart and 12-lead ECG simulator: ecgstudio.app
captions: This is what a heart attack looks like
We block the LAD, the artery on the front of the heart
15 minutes: the T waves grow tall
1 hour: purple is muscle starving for oxygen
The ST segment rises. This is a STEMI
2 days: the T waves flip upside down
1 month: a scar. The Q waves usually stay for life
vo: This is what a heart attack looks like, from the inside.
We block the LAD, the main artery on the front of the heart.
Within minutes, the T waves on the ECG grow tall.
After an hour, the purple area is muscle starving for oxygen...
...and the ST segment rises. That's a STEMI, and the clock is ticking.
By twelve hours, the grey muscle is dying,
and deep Q waves appear.
Two days in, the T waves flip upside down.
A month later it's a scar, and those Q waves usually stay for life.
Try it yourself, free, at ecgstudio.app.

af.title: Atrial fibrillation, then a shock back to normal rhythm
af.post: Atrial fibrillation: the top chambers quiver instead of beating, so the pulse turns irregular. One shock resets every cell and the heart beats as one again. Simulated with ECG Studio, a free 3D heart and 12-lead ECG simulator: ecgstudio.app
captions: This heart is in atrial fibrillation
The top chambers just quiver: hundreds of chaotic signals a minute
So the heartbeat is irregular, and there are no P waves
Every cell resets, and the heart beats as one again
Steady rhythm. The P waves are back
vo: This heart is in atrial fibrillation.
The top chambers aren't beating. They quiver, with hundreds of chaotic signals every minute.
So the heartbeat is irregular, and the P waves are gone.
Shock!
Every cell resets at once, and the heart beats as one again.
A steady rhythm, and the P waves are back.
Normal sinus rhythm.
Try it yourself, free, at ecgstudio.app.

chb.title: Complete heart block: when the top and bottom of the heart stop talking
chb.post: In complete heart block no signal gets from the atria to the ventricles. The P waves keep their own rate, and a slow backup pacemaker drives the ventricles. Simulated with ECG Studio, a free 3D heart and 12-lead ECG simulator: ecgstudio.app
captions: Complete heart block: the top and bottom of the heart stop talking
The small bumps, the P waves, keep a steady 72 a minute
The big spikes come at their own pace, unrelated
A slow backup pacemaker drives the ventricles at 48. This often needs a pacemaker
vo: Complete heart block: the top and bottom of the heart have stopped talking.
The small bumps, the P waves, keep a steady seventy-two a minute...
...but the big spikes come at their own pace, with no connection.
A slow backup pacemaker drives the ventricles at forty-eight. This often needs a pacemaker.
Try it yourself, free, at ecgstudio.app.
